output:
To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Brightline 6% developer off the Kelvin Trade rep is mislabelled (batch LX2291), check your bottles

Some of the Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer, the 1L bottles we've all been buying off the Kelvin Trade rep, is actually 12% (40 vol). Kelvin Trade emailed on Sunday to confirm it: a filling error at the manufacturer, batch LX2291, supplied between 19 October and 5 November. They say other batches and other strengths are fine.

Their email says sorry for any inconvenience. It's a lot more than that. A client of mine got a burn on her scalp from it on Saturday. Aileen had foils roasting on Thursday and thought it was the heater. Both bottles were LX2291.

HOW TO CHECK
- The batch code is on the base of the bottle. It's not on the box, so don't go by the box.
- You're looking for LX2291.
- Check the open ones in your trolley as well as the stock in the back.
- If you can't read the code, don't use it.

WHAT TO DO WITH THEM
Stop using any LX2291 right now. The rep is in on Tuesday and you can hand them back to him, or take them to the Kelvin Trade depot in Hillington. Full credit either way.

If you've had a problem with it, keep one bottle back. Don't bin it and don't hand that one in. Write down the date and what happened, take photos, and put it in the incident book at the desk. Your insurer will want all of that.

WHAT IT DOES
It's double the strength it says on the label, so with bleach it lifts far too fast. Mine was near pale yellow in 18 minutes on a retouch that normally takes 35 to 40. On the scalp it burns. In foils they get hot, and Aileen's lift came out patchy and a bit brassy. If you've used 6% off the rep since 19 October, think back over anything that lifted quicker than it should have.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR
Burning is not the usual tingle. If a client says it's burning, get it off.
- Rinse with cool water, no shampoo, same as Gail's patch test sheet in How We Do Things.
- That sheet points to the NHS page on chemical burns. For a suspected chemical burn it says to phone 999 straight away, not to wait for blistering or bad pain, and to do what the call handler tells you. It says chemical burns need looked at in hospital.
- Gloves on, and take off anything the product has got onto if you can.
- Keep rinsing with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water, for about an hour.
- No creams or anything else on it.
- Trouble breathing, throat swelling or collapse is 999 straight away as well.
- Then write it in the incident book.

NHS page: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/acid-and-chemical-burns/

Any questions, grab me.

Kirsty
